title: Prevent new_bpmn from silently overwriting an existing diagram after restart
description:
## What / impact
`new_bpmn` and Mermaid import autosave to a deterministic filename derived from a process ID and diagram name. `IdGenerator` starts over in every server process, while `commitMutation` defaults to `overwrite=true`. Creating the same-named first diagram after a restart silently replaces the prior file and destroys user data. This is a prerelease blocker.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Point two fresh server/engine instances at the same empty temp diagrams directory.
2. In the first, create a named process, add a task, and stop all state.
3. In the second, create the same name/type and compare IDs, filenames, bytes, and reopened elements.

## Evidence
Two fresh `SimpleBpmnEngine` instances pointed at one temp directory both generated the same process ID and filename. The second `new_bpmn` returned success; reopening that file showed the second empty diagram and the task from the first was gone (`sameId:true`, `sameFilename:true`, `overwritten:true`). Mermaid conversion also resets generator IDs, making equivalent collisions predictable.

## Where
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:100-115, 797-848, 1057-1085, 1298-1308
- src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts ID reset/import path
- src/utils/IdGenerator.ts
- src/utils/FileManager.ts:228-256
- handlers for new_bpmn/new_from_mermaid/open_mermaid_file

## Implementation direction
Do not use process-local counters as persistent file identity. Generate collision-resistant root IDs/filenames or atomically reserve a unique default filename. Make initial creation no-clobber and surface a bounded conflict error; only an explicit, separately validated overwrite operation may replace an existing file. Preserve transactional memory/disk adoption if reservation fails.

## Verification
Add a temp-directory integration/e2e test that creates a populated diagram, disposes/recreates all server state, creates the same name/type again, and asserts the original bytes/elements remain plus a distinct second file. Repeat for new_from_mermaid and concurrent same-name creation. Run persistence, handler, e2e, and package checks.
acceptance_criteria: A new diagram never replaces an existing file unless the caller explicitly opts into overwrite; restart/counter reset cannot collide; a regression test proves the first file is byte-for-byte unchanged and both diagrams remain listable; save_as keeps its no-clobber semantics.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: added UUID-backed storage filenames, atomic no-clobber initial persistence with bounded collision errors, and restart/Mermaid/concurrency regressions preserving original files

title: Model collaboration participants, processes, ownership, and flow scope correctly
description:
## What
Collaboration mutations collapse into one process: participants can serialize as tasks, requested pool size is discarded, nodes have no owner scope, and cross-pool flows cannot be classified. Build collaboration ownership before pool, lane, message-flow, or collaboration layout work.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a collaboration and add a pool with explicit size.
2. Add nodes intended for two pools and connect them.
3. Export and inspect semantic ownership, tags, refs, and DI.

## Where
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts
- src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts
- src/core/DiagramContext.ts
- src/server/tools.ts and handlers.ts
- tests/fixtures/collaboration/

## Implementation
- Add collaboration/process collections, participant.processRef, and node owner/process scope.
- Serialize participants/message flows under collaboration and flow nodes/sequence flows under the owning process.
- Allow element creation to target a scope and reject ambiguous or incompatible ownership.
- Preserve participant position/size and set BPMNPlane to collaboration.
- Define black-box participant behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Adding a pool never emits bpmn:task.
- Two participants own distinct processes with internal sequence flows and one cross-participant message flow.
- Invalid cross-scope sequence flows fail before mutation.
- Ownership, processRef, bounds, and flows survive save/reopen/mutate.

## Verification
- Parse a two-pool fixture with bpmn-moddle and assert owner collections, refs, flow types, and BPMNPlane.
- Import output with bpmn-js or an equivalent renderer smoke test.
- Run npm run type-check and focused collaboration tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adding a pool never emits bpmn:task.
- Two participants own distinct processes with internal sequence flows and one cross-participant message flow.
- Invalid cross-scope sequence flows fail before mutation.
- Ownership, processRef, bounds, and flows survive save/reopen/mutate.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: distinct participant process ownership, scoped sequence/message flows, black-box pools, safe scope rejection, and save/reopen DI round-trips.

title: Replace flat string templates with a schema-aware BPMN document model and serializer
description:
## What
The live engine rebuilds diagrams from a flat element map and silently coerces unsupported BPMN types to tasks. Introduce one typed document model and exhaustive serializer so processes, collaborations, hierarchy, artifacts, references, and BPMN DI remain structurally valid after mutations.

## Where
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts
- src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts
- src/core/DiagramContext.ts
- src/types/index.ts
- src/server/handlers.ts
- tests/unit/core/ and tests/integration/

## Implementation
- Use bpmn-moddle for parse/create/serialize, or a typed intermediate model with exhaustive serializers and no fallback-to-task behavior.
- Represent definitions, processes, collaborations, participants, nested scopes, artifacts, connections, references, and DI separately.
- Replace Map<string, any> domain state with typed discriminated elements and connections carrying owner/scope IDs.
- Centralize XML text/attribute serialization and reference generation.
- Define migration behavior for diagrams already persisted by the string-template engine.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every BPMN type advertised by src/server/tools.ts either serializes to its correct moddle type or is explicitly rejected as unsupported.
- Unknown element/connection types fail without mutating state or files.
- Process and collaboration roots, IDs, refs, and BPMNPlane targets remain correct after add/update/delete/connect operations.
- Names and labels containing all XML metacharacters and Unicode round-trip unchanged.
- Existing supported basic process creation remains compatible.

## Verification
- Add table-driven fixtures for every advertised type and parse each export with bpmn-moddle.
- Round-trip parse -> serialize -> parse and compare semantic types, IDs, refs, and DI.
- Run npm run type-check and focused core/handler Jest suites.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every BPMN type advertised by src/server/tools.ts either serializes to its correct moddle type or is explicitly rejected as unsupported.

title: Path traversal and symlink escape in open/delete file tools and latent FileManager containment bug
description:
## What
open_bpmn, open_mermaid_file, and delete_diagram_file join client input directly beneath the diagrams path and permit traversal/absolute/symlink escapes. save_as currently sanitizes separators, so it is not directly exploitable through filename, but FileManager.validatePath uses an unsafe prefix comparison and its directory-capable API remains a latent escape risk.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a temporary configured diagrams root and an outside sentinel file plus an in-root symlink to it.
2. Call each open/delete entry point with ../, absolute, sibling-prefix, Windows separator/drive/UNC, and symlink forms.
3. Observe outside read/delete access on vulnerable paths; separately verify save_as sanitization and the FileManager sibling-prefix defect.

## Where
src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts loadDiagram() (~lines 374-378) and deleteDiagram() (~lines 383-386); src/server/handlers.ts openMermaidFile() (~lines 158-163) and openBpmn() (~lines 142-146); src/utils/FileManager.ts validatePath() (~lines 69-74) and saveBpmnFile() (~lines 79-137).

## Implementation
- Create one canonical path resolver used by every open/save/save_as/delete/Mermaid file operation.
- Define basename-only or documented relative-path policy; reject absolute paths and enforce extension allowlists.
- Use path.relative with separator-aware containment, never string startsWith.
- Use lstat/realpath policy to reject symlink escapes; for destructive operations document residual race behavior rather than assuming stat-then-unlink is race-free.
- Return bounded errors without exposing sensitive absolute paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No file tool can read, write, or delete outside the configured root through traversal, absolute, sibling-prefix, Windows, or symlink input.
- Valid in-root BPMN/Mermaid operations continue to work.
- Outside sentinels remain unread and unmodified; wrong extensions and empty/dot names reject before I/O.

## Verification
- Run temp-root table tests for POSIX and Windows path forms, sibling-prefix paths, symlinks, empty names, and extension policy.
- Run focused file security tests and npm run type-check.
acceptance_criteria:
- No file tool can read, write, or delete outside the configured root through traversal, absolute, sibling-prefix, Windows, or symlink input.
- Valid in-root BPMN/Mermaid operations continue to work.
- Outside sentinels remain unread and unmodified; wrong extensions and empty/dot names reject before I/O.
notes:
## Prerelease review residual race (2026-08-22)
The basename/extension/symlink checks fixed direct traversal, but the security claim remains incomplete: `resolveSafeFilePath` performs lstat/realpath and returns a pathname, then callers later use ordinary `fs.open`, `fs.rename`, or `fs.unlink`. A local attacker who can mutate the diagrams directory can exchange the checked leaf or parent between validation and use (TOCTOU), reaching a symlink/outside inode.

Where: src/utils/SafeFilePath.ts lines 41-97; src/utils/FileManager.ts lines 137-147 and 220-258; src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts lines 927-938.
Implementation: for reads use no-follow open where supported and compare post-open fstat identity/type to the validated object; for write/delete document and implement a descriptor-relative strategy (`openat`/`renameat`/`unlinkat` via a vetted native boundary) or constrain directory ownership/permissions as an explicit platform policy. Never claim stat-then-use is race-free.
Verification: a synchronized adversarial test swaps the leaf and parent after resolution but before open/rename/unlink; outside sentinels must remain unread/unmodified on each supported platform.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: pinned all BPMN/Mermaid file operations to one root identity with anchored no-follow read, atomic write, and safe delete handling plus synchronized traversal/symlink race regressions

title: Fix production dependency vulnerabilities (1 critical, several high, incl. in @modelcontextprotocol/sdk itself)
description:

title: LABEL_OVERLAP diagnostic checks label vs shape only — label-label overlaps are invisible to the oracle
description: validateShapeAndLabelOverlaps() in tests/helpers/bpmnGeometry.ts compares each label against every shape (node/container), but never compares labels against other labels. Two edge labels — e.g. from adjacent sequence flows or multiple message flows between the same participant pair — can overlap each other without triggering any LABEL_OVERLAP diagnostic. The layout-candidate test matrix therefore cannot surface label-label collisions, leaving a blind spot in the quality gate used to validate the chosen layout library.

title: Geometry oracle missing EDGE_EDGE_CROSSING check — connector criss-crossing goes undetected
description: The fixture geometry validator (tests/helpers/bpmnGeometry.ts) checks SHAPE_OVERLAP, LABEL_OVERLAP (label vs shape), EDGE_SHAPE_COLLISION, and CONTAINMENT_FAILURE, but has no EDGE_EDGE_CROSSING diagnostic. Two connectors can cross each other without triggering any validation failure, so the layout-candidate test matrix reports 'valid geometry' for diagrams that still have criss-crossing edges. This makes it impossible to know whether the chosen layout library (bpmn-auto-layout@2.0.0-alpha.2) actually eliminates edge crossings across the fixture corpus, which is the primary goal of the layout epic.

title: Make auto_layout honest about unsupported vertical layout
description:
## What / impact
The public MCP schema advertises `auto_layout.algorithm` values `horizontal` and `vertical`, but the engine unconditionally throws for vertical. A client can send schema-valid input that always fails as unimplemented, violating the central tool-contract promise and blocking generated clients from knowing supported behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create any current process through the handler.
2. Call auto_layout with algorithm=vertical, which tools/list declares valid.
3. Observe isError:true with the implementation-only-horizontal message.

## Evidence
`handleRequest('auto_layout',{algorithm:'vertical'})` returned `isError:true` with “Only horizontal layout algorithm is currently supported.” The contract suite acknowledges this as a TODO rather than an executable test.

## Where
- src/server/tools.ts:621-629
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:956-963
- src/core/layout/LayoutModel.ts and adapters
- tests/contracts/engine-contract.test.ts:442
- README auto-layout documentation

## Implementation direction
Choose one release scope. Preferred if vertical is required: map it to top-to-bottom layout through the canonical model/adapter and preserve collaboration/lane/waypoint invariants. Otherwise remove vertical from Zod/JSON Schema/TypeScript/docs now and add it back only with tests. Do not keep a knowingly dead enum branch.

## Verification
Assert tools/list schema parity with actual calls. For implementation, run horizontal and vertical golden geometry fixtures including disconnected nodes, cycles, subprocesses, pools/lanes, and message flows; prove dominant direction and no overlaps. For removal, assert vertical rejects at request validation as an unknown value and no docs/types advertise it.
acceptance_criteria: Every algorithm advertised by tools/list succeeds for supported fixture classes and reports its actual direction, or vertical is removed from runtime schema/types/docs until implemented; no valid advertised enum value deterministically returns an implementation error; contract/e2e tests cover the chosen behavior.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: removed unsupported vertical auto-layout from runtime schema/types/docs, deleted the dead engine branch, and added contract/e2e parity coverage for horizontal success and vertical validation rejection

title: Resolve bpmn-js watermark license compliance for headless SVG export
description:
## What / impact
The production SVG exporter embeds bpmn-js 17.11.1 in a headless page and returns `viewer.saveSVG()` output after sanitization. The dependency license has an additional requirement: source responsible for displaying the bpmn.io watermark must not be removed or changed, and the watermark must remain fully visible in an application. The returned SVG contains neither `bpmn.io` nor a watermark. Whether headless export falls within the requirement needs an explicit release decision; shipping without one creates avoidable license/compliance risk.

## Evidence
A real renderer export was 5,030 bytes and contained neither `bpmn.io` nor watermark text. `node_modules/bpmn-js/LICENSE` contains the mandatory watermark clause. Renderer code returns only the saved SVG root and allowlists a limited tag set.

## Where
- package.json/package-lock.json bpmn-js 17.11.1
- src/core/BpmnSvgRenderer.ts:11-13 and 85-195
- tests/integration/svg-export.test.ts
- packaged notices/license documentation

## Implementation direction
Have maintainers/legal choose and document one path: preserve a fully visible bpmn.io watermark in exported SVG and test it; obtain/record a license permitting watermark-free output; or replace bpmn-js rendering with a compatible alternative. If preserving it, update SVG sanitization deliberately without weakening external-resource/XSS controls and include all required notices in the package.

## Verification
Render a real diagram from the packed artifact and assert the chosen compliance invariant (visible safe watermark/link, recorded licensed mode, or no bpmn-js dependency). Review installed license text and npm tarball notices in CI; retain existing SVG safety tests.
acceptance_criteria: A documented maintainer/legal decision confirms the selected renderer and distribution comply with bpmn-js 17.11.1 terms; if bpmn-js remains, required watermark source/visibility is preserved in the served output or a valid alternative license is recorded; an integration test and package audit prevent accidental removal; user docs disclose any attribution behavior.
close_reason: Duplicate of mcp-bpmn-33g.6 created by a review command-substitution failure; all evidence and acceptance criteria are consolidated in mcp-bpmn-33g.6.

title: Reject non-InteractionNode endpoints for BPMN message flows
description:
## What / impact
The engine and semantic validator treat every `bpmn:FlowNode` as a valid message-flow endpoint. BPMN defines message-flow endpoints as `InteractionNode`; gateways do not inherit `InteractionNode`. The server currently creates, serializes, and reports valid collaboration XML containing a message flow attached to a gateway, exporting semantically invalid BPMN.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a collaboration with two white-box participants and one gateway in each process.
2. Connect the gateways with a message flow and export XML.
3. Run full validation and observe the invalid endpoints are accepted with no issue.

## Evidence
A collaboration with gateways in separate participants accepted a message flow, serialized it, and `validate(full)` returned no issue (`serialized:true`, `valid:true`). The bpmn-moddle descriptors show Event, Task, SubProcess, CallActivity, and Participant as InteractionNodes; Gateway is not.

## Where
- src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:143-183 (`assertValidMessageFlowEndpoints`)
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:359-421
- src/core/BpmnValidator.ts:314-342 and 632-634
- tests/integration collaboration/message-flow coverage

## Implementation direction
Centralize an `isInteractionNodeType`/moddle-instance predicate that exactly follows BPMN inheritance and use it in mutation, import normalization, and validation. Keep the existing cross-participant check. Reject invalid endpoints before ID allocation, serialization, or persistence.

## Verification
Table-test every advertised flow-node type as source and target, with positive cases for InteractionNodes and negative gateway cases. Parse/round-trip positive exports with bpmn-moddle; import an invalid gateway message flow and assert a stable validation error code.
acceptance_criteria: Message-flow creation and validation accept only BPMN InteractionNodes and require cross-participant ownership; gateways and other non-InteractionNode FlowNodes reject before mutation; valid task/event/call-activity/subprocess/participant combinations round-trip through bpmn-moddle.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: enforce BPMN InteractionNode message-flow endpoints across mutation, import, and validation with full endpoint matrix coverage

title: Release engine process contexts when diagrams close or are replaced
description:
## What / impact
`close` only clears the public `DiagramContext`; `SimpleBpmnEngine.processes` retains every process ever created or opened for the server lifetime. Switching to another diagram also leaves the prior, now-unaddressable context resident. Imported documents can approach configured byte/element limits, so a client can drive unbounded heap growth and eventual denial of service.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Repeatedly call new_bpmn then close against one handler/engine.
2. Confirm current reports no diagram.
3. Inspect retained process/lock counts or heap and observe growth proportional to all prior diagrams.

## Evidence
After 25 `new_bpmn` + `close` cycles, `diagramContext.hasCurrent()` was false but the engine retained 25 contexts (26 in a combined focused run that included the initial context). The only bulk cleanup API is `engine.clear()`, which the production handler never calls.

## Where
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:57, 100-115, 846-918, 1047-1050
- src/core/DiagramContext.ts:13-78
- src/server/handlers.ts:172-241, 292-309, 853-860

## Implementation direction
Add an engine operation that safely releases a process context and its settled lock without deleting its persisted file. Invoke it after successful close and after switching away from an unaddressable context, coordinated with the context-concurrency fix. Ensure file deletion removes all contexts that reference that filename, not only the first match.

## Verification
Use near-limit imported diagrams and measure retained engine-map size/heap across hundreds of create/open/switch/close cycles. Assert bounded retention, no use-after-release during queued calls, successful reopen from disk, and no leaked processLocks entries.
acceptance_criteria: Closing or replacing the only addressable current diagram releases its engine context and lock after in-flight work drains; repeated create/open/close cycles keep retained contexts bounded; deletion removes every context for the file; persistence and reopen behavior remain unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: release closed/replaced engine contexts and locks, reject queued use-after-release, preserve reopen persistence, and remove every filename-referencing context

title: Serialize context-sensitive MCP calls to prevent current-diagram races
description:
## What / impact
The stdio server dispatches every tools/call directly into one handler while all diagram operations share the mutable singleton `diagramContext`. There is no request queue or explicit diagram ID. Concurrent MCP requests can complete out of arrival order, switch current backwards, mutate the wrong process, or race `close` with a mutation.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Delay completion of the first new_bpmn call.
2. Dispatch it, then dispatch a faster second new_bpmn concurrently through one handler.
3. Observe the first call finishes last and overwrites current selection established by the later invocation.

## Evidence
A focused handler test issued `new_bpmn(first-but-slow)` followed by `new_bpmn(second-but-fast)` concurrently. The second call completed first, but the first later called `setCurrent`, leaving `first-but-slow` current despite the invocation order. Per-process engine locks do not protect the global current-context choice.

## Where
- src/server/index.ts:41-44
- src/server/handlers.ts:119-161 and every diagramContext read/set/clear
- src/core/DiagramContext.ts:13-78
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts process-specific lock implementation

## Implementation direction
Choose one coherent contract: serialize all current-context-sensitive tool calls through a rejection-safe promise queue, or add explicit diagram/process identifiers and make current only a client convenience. If serializing, define whether read-only calls may run concurrently only after their context snapshot is stable. Ensure queue rejection cannot poison later requests.

## Verification
Add a real pipelined JSON-RPC/MCP e2e test with delay-injected create/open/mutate/close calls and deterministic assertions for final current diagram and persisted files. Include a rejected call between successful calls to prove queue liveness and run with open-handle detection.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent context-sensitive calls have a documented deterministic order and cannot act on or restore a stale current diagram; close cannot race a mutation; the serialization mechanism remains live after a rejected call; a pipelined MCP e2e test covers slow/fast create, mutate, and close interleavings.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: FIFO current-diagram request scheduling with safe export read batches, rejection recovery, and pipelined stdio race coverage

title: Upgrade Puppeteer to remediate extract-zip production vulnerability
description:
## What

The required production audit gate now fails with four high-severity findings because puppeteer@24.31.0 resolves @puppeteer/browsers@2.10.13 and extract-zip@2.0.1, which is affected by GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv (unvalidated symlink path traversal). This blocks enabling a green mandatory CI audit in mcp-bpmn-aek.

## Where

package.json and package-lock.json Puppeteer dependency chain, plus SVG/rendering and package smoke coverage that exercises the installed runtime.

## Implementation guidance

Upgrade Puppeteer to a non-vulnerable compatible release (npm audit currently proposes puppeteer@25.8.0 as a breaking change), refresh the lockfile with npm, and verify browser/rendering APIs and supported Node versions rather than applying a forced audit fix blindly. Keep the dependency change scoped and preserve package entrypoint behavior.
acceptance_criteria: npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high exits 0 with no high/critical production findings. Puppeteer-backed rendering and the packaged executable remain functional. npm ci remains deterministic from package-lock.json on the declared Node support range.

title: Add a Ralph implementation loop with Codex recovery for stuck bead closure
description:
## What
Add a repository-local Ralph implementation loop that executes one actionable Beads leaf at a time and recovers automatically when the same bead remains unclosed for three consecutive attempts.

## Where
- ralph-loop/loop.sh
- ralph-loop/PROMPT_build.md
- ralph-loop/tests/loop_test.sh

## Implementation

- Require bd, jq, git, and Codex; use codex exec as the default implementation CLI while retaining AGENT_CMD as an explicit override; select an in-progress non-epic leaf first, otherwise the first ready non-epic leaf, preserving dotted IDs and excluding no-auto-loop/manual-gate labels.

On the third failure for the same bead, run codex exec with a broad prompt to inspect Beads status/dependencies/cycles/orphans/lint/history plus source, tests, and git state; let Codex repair the closure blocker; then reset the counter and return to normal selection.

- Run bash ralph-loop/tests/loop_test.sh; mocked scenarios must cover third-failure Codex escalation and continuation/reset, successful closure without escalation, per-bead failure isolation, dotted IDs, and selector exclusions.

- Failed layout changes neither state nor file.

- Inject layout/parser failure and assert rollback.

The project has two live node-placement paths and two live waypoint emitters. Decide whether to integrate an external layout library or build a typed hand-rolled pipeline. Candidate/version/API claims must be measured, not inferred from volatile package metadata.

## Where

## Decision

## Rationale
Base the choice on the shared fixture matrix, deterministic geometry, mutable-state synchronization, collaboration/lane support, maintenance cost, dependency risk, and runtime compatibility.

## Alternatives Considered
- Official bpmn-auto-layout current release/alpha using its exact documented return contract.
- YABAL at an exact pinned version.
- Older stable bpmn-auto-layout only if its collaboration/message-flow limits satisfy the explicitly narrowed scope.
- Hand-rolled layered layout using the canonical IR and complete phase/dependency plan.

## Decision Criteria
- Process, branch/rejoin, cycle, self-loop, skip edge, labels, collaboration/message flow, lanes, and in-scope subprocess/boundary fixtures.
- Valid complete DI, deterministic repeated runs, semantic ID/extension preservation, and state synchronization after later mutations.
- Node/runtime/dependency compatibility, warnings/unsupported behavior, performance, maintenance, and rollback.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact candidates, versions, APIs, retrieval date, and fixture outcomes are recorded.
- One option is selected with explicit rejected alternatives and evidence.
- The selected implementation bead is unblocked; non-selected branch beads are superseded with the chosen bead.
- Scope does not claim collaboration support using malformed single-process Mermaid pool fixtures.

## Verification

- Confirm package engines/dependencies with npm metadata and a clean install.
- Prototype create -> layout -> mutate -> export to test state preservation before closing.
design:
Decision (retrieved 2026-08-22)

Select the official bpmn-auto-layout package at exactly 2.0.0-alpha.2 (npm dist-tag next) behind a local typed adapter. Call layoutProcess(xml); consume the documented Promise result { xml, warnings }; treat exported LayoutError rejections and warnings as bounded unsupported behavior. Pin the exact prerelease in production rather than using a range or dist-tag.

Supported scope is limited to the measured corpus: sequential process, branch/rejoin, skip flow, cycle, self-loop, long labels, a valid two-process collaboration with message flow, lanes, and the in-scope expanded subprocess/boundary-event case. All nine produced complete oracle-valid DI and deterministic normalized output across two runs. This does not assert support for arbitrary BPMN constructs. Unknown or unsupported input must surface adapter warnings/errors, and output remains subject to the independent geometry oracle.

Constraints: Node >=18 (project >=18.14.1); dependencies bpmn-moddle ^10.0.0 and min-dash ^5.0.0; ESM and CJS exports are present; the package publishes no TypeScript declarations. The adapter must therefore own a minimal local contract and isolate the unstable prerelease API. The selected package is official bpmn.io but remains an alpha. Rollback is removal/replacement of the adapter and exact dependency; the canonical LayoutModel and fixture oracle remain package-neutral.

Rejected alternatives:
- bpmn-auto-layout 1.3.0: rejects project scope because collaboration lays out only the first participant and omits message-flow/second-process DI; lane DI and nested subprocess geometry also fail.
- yet-another-bpmn-auto-layout 2.0.0: collaboration passes, but lane shapes are missing and subprocess/boundary geometry fails; it also adds graph-by-ivan-tulaev ^1.0.0-alpha.16.

- bpmn-auto-layout 1.3.0 with narrowed scope: rejected because narrowing away collaboration, lanes, and subprocess/boundary behavior contradicts the epic corpus.

State preservation: the create -> selected layout -> mutable rename -> export prototype preserves all semantic IDs, an opaque extension element, and byte-equivalent normalized library-generated shapes and waypoints. The existing mcp-bpmn-3g8.3 remains responsible for production DI synchronization during integration.

The explicitly hand-roll-only beads mcp-bpmn-7hm, mcp-bpmn-ynt, mcp-bpmn-b2o, mcp-bpmn-qxx, mcp-bpmn-amd, mcp-bpmn-gt3, mcp-bpmn-tyy, and mcp-bpmn-317 are superseded by mcp-bpmn-97u. description:
## What

- Reject layout above benchmark-derived element/edge/density limits before synchronous work, or isolate it in a cancellable worker/child process.
- Build adjacency maps once per request/context for element listing.
- Add stable ordering, default/max limit, offset/cursor, and hasMore to list_elements and list_diagrams; document response compatibility.
- Benchmark sparse and dense graphs to set limits rather than using an arbitrary 600-node constant.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact-limit inputs succeed and one-over inputs reject without excessive memory/latency.
- Synchronous pathological layout cannot hang the server beyond the documented budget.
- Pagination is stable with correct hasMore for empty, sparse, dense, and final pages.

title: placeMessageLabel does not treat peer message-flow labels as obstacles — labels can overlap each other
description: routeCollaborationConnections() in src/core/layout/CollaborationLayoutPolicy.ts builds labelObstacles from element and lane bounds (lines 303-307) but does not include the label bounds of already-routed message flows. When multiple message flows exist between the same pair of participants, their labels are placed independently using the same candidate set (midpoints along the same horizontal/vertical segments), so they will often land on identical or near-identical positions. The placeMessageLabel fallback (line 384-391) places the label at outer.right + gap, which means all fallback labels also stack at the same coordinate. Fix: accumulate placed label bounds into labelObstacles before each subsequent call.

title: AnchoredFileWorker: 100ms idle timeout causes constant subprocess churn under normal load
description: The ANCHORED_FILE_WORKER inline script in src/utils/SafeFilePath.ts arms a 100ms idle exit timer after each operation and on startup. At any inter-request gap longer than 100ms the worker process exits, and the next file operation (read, write, delete) must restart it and wait for the ready handshake before proceeding. Under normal MCP usage where diagram operations arrive more than 100ms apart, every file operation effectively cold-starts the worker. The SafeFileStore.workerFor() and runWithRetry() mechanics hide the restart, but the latency penalty and process churn are real. Increasing the idle timeout to ~5 s (or making it configurable via the ResourceLimits struct) would eliminate most restarts without holding resources open for long.

title: BpmnSvgRenderer: new browser process per render call — no reuse across exports
description: BpmnSvgRenderer.render() calls this.launchBrowser() every invocation (src/core/BpmnSvgRenderer.ts:65) and closes the browser in the finally block of renderWithBrowser() (line 98). Each Puppeteer browser launch takes 1–3 seconds. For an AI agent workflow that exports SVG repeatedly (e.g. after each diagram edit), every export pays full browser-start overhead. The maxConcurrentRenders=1 default serialises renders, so the overhead compounds. Keeping a long-lived browser page alive between renders (launching lazily on first call, reusing the existing browser until close() is called) would reduce per-export latency by roughly 90% for warm calls.

title: CollaborationLayoutPolicy: shapeFor/edgeFor do O(n) linear scan inside message-flow routing loop
description: routeCollaborationConnections() in src/core/layout/CollaborationLayoutPolicy.ts calls shapeFor() and edgeFor() for every connection it routes (lines 347, 350). Each helper does Array.from(document.diagram.shapes.values()).find(...), an O(M) scan over all DI shapes. For a collaboration with N message flows and M total shapes, routing is O(N×M). For a diagram near the configured limits (2000 elements, many message flows), this can become slow. Build a Map<elementId, shape> and Map<connectionId, edge> once before the loop and replace .find() calls with O(1) Map lookups.

title: Handle SIGTERM with bounded graceful shutdown and in-flight cleanup
description:
## What / impact
The executable handles SIGINT only. Containers, service managers, and `npm` commonly terminate with SIGTERM. Under SIGTERM Node exits by signal immediately, with no server/transport close, no bounded drain of active autosave operations, and no coordinated cleanup of Puppeteer/layout subprocesses. This risks partial user-visible operations and orphaned child processes.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Spawn the built stdio server and complete MCP initialize.
2. Send SIGTERM to the child process.
3. Observe exit by signal with no shared shutdown/drain path; repeat during a delayed child-backed operation.

## Evidence
After MCP initialize, sending SIGTERM to the server produced `{code:null, signal:'SIGTERM'}`. No shutdown hook ran; src/server/index.ts installs only `process.on('SIGINT')`.

## Where
- src/server/index.ts:41-65
- BpmnSvgRenderer browser lifecycle
- src/core/layout/BpmnLayoutAdapter.ts subprocess lifecycle
- tests/e2e server process harness

## Implementation direction
Implement one idempotent shutdown coordinator for SIGINT, SIGTERM, transport close/EOF, and fatal startup errors. Stop accepting calls, await tracked in-flight handlers and their persistence, close server/transport/renderers/layout children, then exit; enforce a documented hard timeout and meaningful nonzero exit on forced shutdown. Avoid calling process.exit before awaited cleanup settles.

## Verification
Spawn the real built server, begin delay-injected save/layout/render calls, send SIGTERM and SIGINT, and assert deterministic exit codes, committed-or-rolled-back files, closed pipes/browser/layout child PIDs, no open handles, and safe behavior on two rapid signals and startup failure.
acceptance_criteria: SIGINT, SIGTERM, transport EOF, and startup failure use one idempotent shutdown path; accepted in-flight mutations finish or roll back before exit within a documented timeout; renderer/layout child processes are closed; repeated signals cannot double-close; process-level tests assert clean exit and no orphan children.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: unified bounded shutdown drains accepted persistence, closes renderer/layout children, handles SIGINT/SIGTERM/EOF/startup failure idempotently, and has process-level coverage

title: Enforce XML NCName rules for every BPMN xsd:ID
description:
## What / impact
BPMN IDs are XML Schema `xsd:ID`, whose lexical space is NCName (no colon, valid start/continuation characters). The serializer, importer, engine element IDs, and validator currently enforce uniqueness/references but not NCName syntax. They can emit and bless XML that downstream BPMN tools reject or cannot reference reliably.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create/import a BPMN element whose ID is a:b.
2. Serialize and reopen the document.
3. Run syntax/semantic/full validation and observe no invalid-xsd-ID issue.

## Evidence
Creating an element with `id:'a:b'` succeeded; export contained the ID, bpmn-moddle parsed it, and all validator levels returned no issue (`serialized:true`, `syntaxValid:true`, `issues:[]`). The existing QName helper is only for callable references and intentionally allows one colon, so it cannot validate IDs.

## Where
- src/core/BpmnDocument.ts ID import/serialization and existing NCName character ranges at lines 74-103
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:120-132 and generated/internal IDs
- src/core/BpmnValidator.ts syntax/reference indexing
- src/server/tools.ts `bpmnId` versus generic `identifier`
- DI IDs, lanes, connections, root definitions, and event-definition IDs

## Implementation direction
Create one XML-1.0 NCName predicate (without a QName colon) and apply it to every semantic and DI ID at document ingress, public creation, generated-ID assertion, and validation. Include path/type in errors. Do not silently sanitize imported IDs because that can break references; reject or implement an explicit whole-document migration.

## Verification
Build a table from NCName boundaries: colon, spaces, leading digits/dash/dot, empty, combining marks, valid non-ASCII starts, supplementary code points, and malformed surrogates. Cover every ID-bearing document collection and DI reference, mutation rollback, import/export/reopen, and downstream moddle/tool interoperability.
acceptance_criteria: Every authored or imported semantic/DI ID satisfies XML Schema NCName and is unique before serialization; invalid IDs such as a:b reject with a stable path-aware error and no mutation; valid Unicode NCNames round-trip; validation flags legacy invalid files rather than declaring them syntax-valid.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: enforced XML 1.0 NCName and uniqueness across authored/imported semantic and DI IDs, added stable validation and Unicode round-trip support, and passed npm run test:all

title: Upgrade implicit Mermaid endpoints when a later explicit node declaration appears
description:
## What / impact
Mermaid edges may introduce nodes before their explicit declaration. `MermaidParser.addNode` stores the first implicit placeholder and, when it later sees the explicit declaration, emits `DUPLICATE_NODE` without replacing or merging the node. The converter therefore loses the user's label and shape and may map the wrong BPMN type.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Parse `flowchart TD\n  A --> B((End))\n  A[Actual label]`.
2. Inspect node A and parser warnings.
3. Observe the implicit label/type remain and the first explicit declaration is reported as a duplicate.

## Evidence
For `flowchart TD; A --> B((End)); A[Actual label]`, node A remained `{ id:'A', type:'process', label:'A' }` and diagnostics included `DUPLICATE_NODE`. Mermaid's normal declaration order should make A an explicitly labeled task, not an unnamed implicit placeholder.

## Where
- src/converters/MermaidParser.ts:243-307 and 431-453
- src/converters/ASTTypes.ts / MermaidConverter.ts node mapping
- tests/unit/converters and tests/integration/mermaid-conversion-edge-cases.test.ts

## Implementation direction
Track whether each stored node is implicit or explicit. On the first later explicit declaration, replace/merge the placeholder and update its source location while preserving edge/subgraph references. Warn only when a node already has an explicit definition; define deterministic handling for conflicting repeated declarations.

## Verification
Add declaration-order permutations for every supported Mermaid shape, labels/classes/subgraphs, and genuine duplicate explicit declarations. Assert AST values, warning codes/locations, BPMN types/names, node counts, and stable round-trip XML.
acceptance_criteria: A later explicit declaration supplies the node label, shape/type, class, and source location for a prior implicit edge endpoint; genuine repeated explicit declarations still produce one deterministic duplicate diagnostic; conversion output and statistics contain one node.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: implicit Mermaid endpoints upgrade in place from the first explicit declaration, with deterministic duplicate diagnostics and single-node BPMN conversion coverage

title: Fix npm test dropping configured Jest exclusions
description:
## What

Do not add e2e to the shared jest.config.js exclusion because npm run test:all must continue exercising e2e after a clean build. ## Acceptance Criteria

title: Choose portable BPMN versus an executable vendor extension dialect
description:
## Context
The API advertises assignee, candidate groups, and due dates while documentation claims generic BPMN compliance. These require a named extension dialect/version or a portable metadata policy.

## Where
- src/server/tools.ts activity/update schemas
- serializer/import model
- README.md and IMPLEMENTATION.md
- target engine/modeler tests

## Decision
Select and document one supported option using the criteria below.

## Rationale
Record evidence for the selected option, rejected options, compatibility impact, and follow-up dependencies.

## Alternatives Considered
- Portable BPMN core plus preserved opaque extensions.
- Camunda 7 profile.
- Camunda 8/Zeebe profile.
- Flowable/Activiti profile.
- Multi-profile API only if maintenance cost is justified.

## Decision Criteria
- Target parser/modeler interoperability.
- Namespace/version stability and typed API ergonomics.
- Portable-mode behavior and unknown-extension preservation.
- No arbitrary XML namespace/attribute injection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Decision names profile(s), namespace URIs, versions, typed fields, and compatibility guarantees.
- Portable behavior and unknown imported extension handling are explicit.
- Property feature beads depend on this decision.

## Verification
- Generate representative user tasks for shortlisted profiles and import into target modeler/parser.
- Record exact versions and fixture outcomes in decision notes.
design: Selected portable as the default document profile and camunda7 as the only opt-in executable-extension profile. Camunda 7 namespace: http://camunda.org/schema/1.0/bpmn. Tested contract: bpmn-moddle 9.0.2 plus camunda-bpmn-moddle 7.0.1. Allowlisted UserTask fields for mcp-bpmn-g7s: assignee string, candidateGroups string array serialized comma-separated, and dueDate string; update null removes a field. Portable mode rejects these fields and emits no vendor namespace. Unknown warning-free imported extensions remain opaque and are semantically retained; arbitrary namespace, QName, attribute, and raw XML authoring are forbidden. Profile selection applies to all authored creation paths, open_bpmn detects actual namespace use with descriptor reparse, and current plus creation/open results report extensionProfile. Parser compatibility is guaranteed only for the exact tested versions, not Camunda deployment, execution, rendering, or modeler releases.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision names profile(s), namespace URIs, versions, typed fields, and compatibility guarantees.
- Portable behavior and unknown imported extension handling are explicit.
- Property feature beads depend on this decision.
notes: Verification on 2026-08-22 with Node 25.9.0: portable-user-task.bpmn parsed humanPerformer and potentialOwner with zero bpmn-moddle 9.0.2 warnings and retained exact types/expressions through descriptor round-trip and unrelated MCP-BPMN mutation. camunda7-user-task.bpmn parsed assignee, candidateGroups, and dueDate with zero warnings using bpmn-moddle 9.0.2 plus camunda-bpmn-moddle 7.0.1; all fields survived descriptor round-trip and unrelated MCP-BPMN mutation. description:

title: Layout subprocess runner uses falsy short-circuit for error.code — can silently drop real error codes
description: The inline runner script in BpmnAutoLayoutV2Adapter.loadSelectedLayoutInSubprocess (src/core/layout/BpmnLayoutAdapter.ts:209) uses the expression 'error && error.code || "LAYOUT_FAILED"'. If error.code is 0, false, null, or any other falsy non-undefined value, the expression silently falls back to 'LAYOUT_FAILED' and the real error code is lost. Downstream callers (BpmnLayoutError, normalizeLayoutError) that switch on error.code will miss the actual cause. Replace with nullish coalescing: error?.code ?? 'LAYOUT_FAILED' (and similarly for error.message on line 211).

title: Math.min/max spread pattern over mapped arrays is fragile — fails if arrays exceed ~65k items
description: Several layout functions spread a mapped array directly into Math.min/Math.max: calculateLayoutBounds (src/core/layout/LayoutModel.ts:245-248), updateContainerBounds/layoutWithPools in LayoutEngine (src/core/LayoutEngine.ts:82-87, 264-267), findMinPossibleLevel (LayoutEngine.ts:222-223), normalizeGeometry in bpmnGeometry (tests/helpers/bpmnGeometry.ts:194-203). Node.js throws 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' when more than ~65k arguments are spread. Current resource limits (maxLayoutElements=2000) keep actual counts well below this threshold, but the pattern is a silent footgun: any operator raising the limit above ~32k elements would hit the crash. All spread-into-Math calls should be replaced with .reduce() or equivalent iteration.

## Evidence
The tools mapping at src/server/tools.ts:671-675 sets only inputSchema; handlers return `content` but never `structuredContent`. list/get/current/validate already construct JSON objects before stringifying, while new/add/connect results omit stable machine-readable IDs.

## Where

- src/types/index.ts public result shapes
- contract/e2e tools/list and tools/call assertions

## Implementation direction
Define minimal per-tool output schemas beside input schemas and return the same object in `structuredContent`; retain text content for compatibility. Start with query/export metadata and all creation/mutation tools where generated identifiers are required for subsequent calls. Keep binary/embedded SVG content in MCP content while exposing safe metadata structurally. Validate outputs in tests or a shared boundary.

## Verification
For every advertised tool, call the real server and validate structuredContent against outputSchema, including defaults, pagination, validation issues, generated IDs, XML/SVG metadata, and error responses. Confirm existing text-only clients continue to receive useful content.
